title: Real-world growth outcomes and safety of vosoritide in children with achondroplasia: a Brazilian single center 24 monhts experience.
abstract: To evaluate the longitudinal effects of vosoritide on growth, body proportionality, and safety in children with achondroplasia in a real-world clinical setting, and to identify early predictors of treatment response. We conducted a hybrid retrospective-prospective observational study in children with achondroplasia treated with vosoritide at a single tertiary center. Thirty-five children (mean age 5.92 ± 3.56 years) were included. Height velocity increased significantly at both 12 months (+1.50 SDS) and 24 months (+1.91 SDS) compared with baseline (p < 0.001). Vosoritide increased linear growth in this real-world cohort, with heterogeneous response patterns over time.

title: Once-weekly somapacitan enhances linear growth in girls with Turner syndrome: a randomized controlled phase 3 study.
abstract: Non-inferiority for once-weekly somapacitan vs. daily GH for the primary endpoint, HV at week 52, was confirmed. Once-weekly somapacitan showed non-inferiority and is comparable to daily GH after 52 weeks of treatment in enhancing linear growth while maintaining IGF-I concentrations within a similar range in treatment-naïve girls with TS.

journal.title: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

title: Modified-Release Hydrocortisone for Female Fertility in Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia.
abstract: MRHC improved hormonal control and was associated with restoration of menstrual cyclicity and high rates of spontaneous conception with a lower hydrocortisone dose equivalent. Circadian optimization of GC therapy by MRHC may represent a paradigm shift in fertility management in females with CAH.

journal.title: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

title: Physiology and diagnostic potential of beta-hydroxybutyrate in neonatal glycemia - a prospective cohort study.
abstract: Neonates with hypoglycemia risk factors and those receiving formula developed less ketonemia. The low overall incidence of ketonemia and its dependence on feeding regimen limit the utility of BOHB, alone or in combination with BG, as a broadly applicable marker for determining when hypoglycemia screening can be safely discontinued.

journal.title: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

title: Prenatal care for Disorders/Differences of Sex Development: 10-years look back in an expert-center.
abstract: Prenatal assessment may support counselling and care planning for families expecting a child with DSD. Further prospective studies are necessary to confirm these findings and formulate recommendations for prenatal management of DSD.

journal.title: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

title: Temporal stability of cardiometabolic risk factors from the perspective of primordial disease prevention in children.
abstract: Individualised biomarker screening at low FPR misclassifies the majority of children who will have high values as adults (low statistical feasibility). Biomarker tracking is more useful for guiding broad population-based primordial prevention programmes.

journal.title: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

title: Ketone Profiles in Community-Dwelling Adults with Type 1 Diabetes Using Continuous Ketone Monitoring.
abstract: Most community-dwelling adults with type 1 diabetes have ketones <0.6 mmol/L. Glucose levels rose with elevated ketones but were not a diagnostic substitute.

abstract: [Abstract not available]

title: Use of Automated Insulin Delivery Systems Following Pediatric Total Pancreatectomy and Islet Auto Transplantation.
abstract: AID use after TPIAT can maintain tight glycemic control without hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia and may be considered for use in post-TPIAT glycemic management.

title: Safety and Feasibility of Algorithmic Continuous Glucose Monitoring-Based Titration in People with Type 2 Diabetes Using Insulin Degludec.
abstract: Using CGM and receiving algorithmic CGM-based titrations were feasible, safe, and had favorable overall glycemic metrics.

title: Standardizing the Accuracy and Performance Evaluation Metrics of Integrated Continuous Glucose Monitors in the Asia-Pacific Region.
abstract: Harmonizing iCGM regulatory standards in APAC is anticipated to enhance device accuracy, safety, and interoperability, improve diabetes care, and streamline regulatory processes.

title: Glycemic Outcomes Following a Missed Premeal Bolus: A Comparative Study of Three Automated Insulin Delivery Systems in Children with Type 1 Diabetes.
abstract: 780G and CIQ outperformed CamAPS in limiting postprandial hyperglycemia, suggesting they may be preferable for children with diabetes prone to bolus omission.

title: MiniMed780G Hybrid Closed-Loop Systems Improves Markers of Vascular and Endothelial Function in Patients with Type 1 Diabetes.
abstract: MiniMed780G HCLS demonstrated superiority over MDI or SGLT-2i in terms of glycemic control and cardiovascular function in T1D.

title: Recommendations from the United Kingdom UNBIASED Study to Address Diabetes Technology Access Disparities for Children and Young People.
abstract: This UK UNBIASED study highlights the urgent need for standardized policies, increased awareness campaigns, culturally tailored education, peer support initiatives, and improved health care provider training to ensure equitable access to diabetes technology for all CYP with T1D.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Oral GLP-1 RA Orforglipron on Weight and Glycemic Control According to Diabetes Status: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Orforglipron demonstrated clinically meaningful metabolic benefits with an acceptable safety profile.

title: Inhaled Technosphere Insulin in Children with Diabetes: The INHALE-1 Extension Study.
abstract: The INHALE-1 extension phase showed no safety concerns. TI may be a useful treatment option for some pediatric patients with diabetes, particularly for those who choose not to or are unable to use an AID system.

title: Association of Continuous Glucose Monitoring Metrics with Incident Diabetic Retinopathy: A Real-World Long-Term Study.
abstract: CGM metrics provide more informative risk stratification than HbA1c alone for diabetic retinopathy risk.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Retinal Biomarkers for Detecting Type 2 Diabetes and Prediabetes Among Asian Indians [DART Study].
abstract: AI-informed retinal venous features on routine fundus images could potentially serve as noninvasive DM detection using AI models among Asian Indians.

title: Performance of the Fifth Generation of a 16-Day Continuous Glucose Monitoring System in Adults with Diabetes.
abstract: The system demonstrated accurate glucose measurements across the 16-day wear period, irrespective of sensor placement site or glucose concentration.

title: Automated Insulin Delivery Associated with Superior Glycemic Outcomes in Type 1 Diabetes: A Swedish National Registry Analysis.
abstract: AID use was consistently associated with clinically and statistically significant HbA1c reductions in adults with T1D, with the greatest effect for Tandem Control-IQ technology.

title: Consistent Benefit of Control-IQ+ Automated Insulin Delivery Across a Range of Characteristics of Adults with Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: The glycemic benefit of AID was observed across a wide range of participant characteristics, and AID should be a consideration for all adults with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes.

title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Systems in Noninsulin-Treated People with Type 2 Diabetes: Erratum.
abstract: [Abstract not available]

title: Ensuring Equitable Access to Diabetes Technology for People with Disabilities.
abstract: [Abstract not available]

title: Perioperative Blood Glucose Control following Implementation of Standardized Protocols in Children and Adolescents with Diabetes Undergoing Surgery.
abstract: [Abstract not available]

title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Metrics in Women with Type 2 Diabetes in Pregnancy: The TIMELY Observational Cohort Study.
abstract: Several glycemic metrics, including TIRp and mean glucose, were associated with large-for-gestational-age infants. Early pregnancy or preconception glucose optimization may be necessary to improve outcomes.

title: The Viral Legacy in Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Impact of Concurrent Respiratory Viral Infections on Acute Severity and Long-Term Glycemic Control in Children With Newly Diagnosed Type 1 Diabetes.
abstract: Concurrent respiratory viral infections significantly increase DKA acute severity, exacerbate pancreatic β-cell dysfunction, and impair long-term glycemic control in newly diagnosed pediatric T1DM, highlighting the need for prioritized virus screening, prevention, and optimized individualized treatment.

journal.title: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology

title: Off-Label Use of Teriparatide for Osteotomy Healing in an Adolescent with Osteogenesis Imperfecta Type VIII: A Case Report.
abstract: This case represents the first documented use of teriparatide to promote osteotomy healing in an adolescent with OI. The favourable clinical and radiologic outcome suggests a potential role for anabolic therapy in managing complex bone healing challenges in paediatric OI.

journal.title: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology

title: Risk Factors for Cerebral Edema in Pediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Observational Studies.
abstract: Bicarbonate administration may be associated with cerebral edema, which is consistent with current recommendations against its routine use in pediatric DKA. Evidence about younger age, new-onset diabetes, and severe metabolic phenotype remains very uncertain.

journal.title: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology

title: Striking Scrotal Hyperpigmentation as an Early Clinical Sign of Familial Glucocorticoid Deficiency Type 2: A Case with Homozygous MRAP Variant.
abstract: This case highlights striking neonatal scrotal hyperpigmentation as a potential early clinical clue suggestive of familial glucocorticoid deficiency, even when newborn screening for CAH is normal.

journal.title: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology

title: Menstrual Health in Adolescents with Congenital Heart Disease.
abstract: Adolescents with CHD have menstrual characteristics comparable to those of healthy controls, but may differ in their perception and tolerance of menstrual symptoms.

journal.title: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology

title: Prolactinoma Associated with L-Dopa-Resistant Hyperprolactinemia in a Child with Tetrahydropterin (BH4) Deficiency.
abstract: In patients with BH4 deficiency, hyperprolactinemia resistant to L-dopa therapy may indicate the development of prolactinoma; regular laboratory follow-up and cranial imaging are clinically important.

abstract: [Abstract not available]

abstract: [Abstract not available]

title: Updated Dutch 2026 Pediatric Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma Guideline: Aligning with Europe.
abstract: The 2026 Dutch guideline aligns with European recommendations while preserving context-specific adaptations, providing a framework for consistent, patient-centered care.

title: Identification and Follow-up of At-Risk Children Mitigate Disease Severity and Improve Treatment Outcomes in Type 1 Diabetes.
abstract: DIPP participants had a milder clinical presentation at T1D diagnosis, with lower HbA1c levels and lower insulin requirements during the first year.

title: Long-term Effect of C-Peptide Level on Clinical Outcomes in the Scottish Type 1 Bioresource Cohort.
abstract: These data demonstrate the importance of C-peptide level and its maintenance for glycemic control and avoidance of acute and chronic complications of T1D.

title: DiaBetter Together: Outcomes of a Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating a Peer Mentor Behavioral Intervention for Young Adults With Type 1 Diabetes During the Transfer From Pediatric to Adult Care.
abstract: DiaBetter Together produced modest benefits for psychosocial outcomes during the challenging transfer period, although glycemic, behavioral, and transfer improvements remain difficult to achieve.

title: In Utero Exposure to Preexisting or Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Increases Incidence of Diabetes in the Children of First Nations and Non-First Nations Mothers: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Exposure to preexisting diabetes or gestational diabetes mellitus in utero was associated with an increased incidence of diabetes in children and young adults, with a stronger association among First Nations people.

title: Energy drink ban: putting children's health first.
abstract: [Abstract not available]

title: Perceptions and Psychological Adverse Effects of Central Precocious Puberty or Early Normal Puberty, and Its Treatment Among Affected Girls and Their Caregivers.
abstract: Girls and their caregivers lacked adequate knowledge of iCPP/ENP. Given that psychological stress was associated with iCPP/ENP, screening for psychological stress should be considered as part of caring for these patients.

title: Diagnosis of Growth Hormone Deficiency in Children: Comparative Performance of Arginine Versus Glucagon as the First Stimulation Test.
abstract: GST is associated with a lower rate of discordant results compared to AST and potentially reduces the need for a second test, minimising patient inconvenience, lowering healthcare expenses, and decreasing time-consuming hospital visits for families.

title: Transient Hyperparathyroidism and Severe Intrauterine Osteopenia Linked to Novel Homozygous TRPV6 Deletion.
abstract: The TRPV6-p.Arg492* mutation affects maternal-foetal calcium transport and explains the observed phenotype of skeletal abnormalities and hyperparathyroidism.

title: Pituitary Magnetic Resonance Imaging as a Prognostic Factor of Pituitary Insufficiency-The Follow-Up Analysis of a Cohort of Children With Pituitary Stalk Interruption Syndrome.
abstract: Children with PSIS require repeated reassessment of pituitary function if combined pituitary hormone deficiency is not present at initial evaluation, as progression may occur over time.

title: Bardet-Biedl Syndrome in India: Genotypic Spectrum and Clinical Features From a Single-Centre Cohort.
abstract: This study provides descriptive insights into the genotypic spectrum of BBS in an Indian cohort, with frequent involvement of BBS10 and BBS2, underscoring the importance of population-specific genetic data.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Analogue Therapy in Central Precocious Puberty: A Comparative Analysis of Obese and Normal-Weight Girls.
abstract: GnRHa therapy had a beneficial effect on height gain in both CPP girls with overweight/obesity and normal weight; BMI SDSs at final height were less than those at diagnosis in both groups.

title: Maternal-Neonatal Metabolic Continuity and Early Postnatal HPG Axis Activity in Healthy Term Neonates.
abstract: Maternal metabolic markers were associated with neonatal metabolic parameters but were not strongly associated with early neonatal gonadotropin levels in this cohort.

title: Endocrine Phenotypes and Hormonal Treatment in Meier-Gorlin Syndrome: Report of Two Cases and a Systematic Review of Literature.
abstract: MGORS should be kept in mind as a differential of multiple endocrinopathies. Cases should undergo screening for growth hormone deficiency; response to GH has been reported in some individuals, particularly where GHD or delayed bone age was present.

title: The Spectrum of Congenital Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism: A 30-Year Experience at a Tertiary Paediatric Centre.
abstract: CHH is a heterogeneous group of disorders, with varying prevalence of associated comorbidities according to diagnostic subtypes; areas remain for further research in diagnostics and therapeutics of CHH in the paediatric age group.

title: A randomised clinical trial testing the safety of and metabolic responses to short-term duodenal infusion of recombinant RORDEP1 in healthy men.
abstract: Short-term duodenal infusion of r-RORDEP1 is safe and well tolerated and elicits changes in plasma incretins, insulin and glucose, and whole-body insulin sensitivity, aligning with rodent findings.

title: Effect of somatostatin receptor 2 antagonism on glucagon counterregulation during a hyperinsulinaemic euglycaemic-hypoglycaemic glucose clamp in adult men and women with long-standing type 1 diabetes: a randomised crossover phase 1 study.
abstract: Administration of the SSTR2 antagonist ZT-01 increased glucagon responsiveness during insulin-induced hypoglycaemia in individuals with type 1 diabetes.

title: SGLT2 inhibitor use and disparities in all-cause mortality in type 2 diabetes: insights from a multi-ethnic population.
abstract: The protective effect of SGLT2i use on mortality appears to differ by ethnicity and is greater in Indigenous Māori and Pacific populations in New Zealand with type 2 diabetes.

title: A narrative systematic review of definitions and diagnostic criteria for disordered eating and eating disorders in type 1 diabetes.
abstract: This systematic review highlights the lack of a unified, evidence-based definition of type 1 diabetes and disordered eating, resulting in inconsistent screening, diagnostic and reporting practices; findings provide a foundation for an international consensus definition. Note: this review explicitly excluded paediatric studies.

title: pFIB scores for paediatric MASLD fibrosis are associated with risk of youth-onset type 2 diabetes in children with obesity.
abstract: A liver-derived composite risk score identifies a subgroup of adolescents with obesity at markedly increased short-term risk of type 2 diabetes, suggesting integration of hepatic and metabolic variables may improve early risk stratification in paediatric obesity.

title: Early-onset juvenile Paget disease associated with a homozygous intronic TNFRSF11B variant: a 2-year follow-up.
abstract: Early bisphosphonate therapy effectively improved skeletal disease activity in juvenile Paget disease, but extraskeletal manifestations may still occur during follow-up, highlighting the need for continued long-term surveillance.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Post-COVID-19 rise in central precocious puberty: an integrative Review.
abstract: A cautious integrative model may help reconcile the strong female predominance and temporal association with lockdown-related exposures in pandemic-era CPP, while defining testable priorities for future cohort, exposure, and mechanistic studies.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Association between hyperchloremia and outcomes of children admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA).
abstract: Hyperchloremia in children with DKA is associated with delayed recovery and prolonged PICU stay. Lower body weight and 0.9% NaCl use increase hyperchloremia risk.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Iodine status and thyroid function in children with multiple food allergy: a prospective cross-sectional study.
abstract: Children with multiple food allergies receiving elimination diets are at increased risk of mild iodine deficiency, even in iodine-sufficient regions, although overt thyroid dysfunction may not yet be evident.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Clinical characteristics and endocrine outcomes of functional and nonfunctional adrenal lesions in children: a single-center cohort study.
abstract: Functional adrenal lesions in the pediatric population are characterized by larger tumor size, distinct hormonal secretion patterns, and specific clinical manifestations, facilitating early differentiation from nonfunctional lesions.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Early metabolic and hepatic alterations in children with Down syndrome: a hidden risk beyond BMI.
abstract: Children and adolescents with Down syndrome display an early high-risk cardiometabolic phenotype only partly reflected by BMI, supporting broader metabolic surveillance in pediatric DS.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: A comparative analysis of all reported patients with MTHFS-related neurodevelopmental disorder.
abstract: MTHFS deficiency should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with severe developmental delay and microcephaly accompanied by isolated hyperhomocysteinemia.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Clinical course of Graves' orbitopathy in children with newly diagnosed hyperthyroidism: a prospective observational study.
abstract: In pediatric hyperthyroidism, Graves' orbitopathy is usually mild and inactive, with rare short-term clinical progression, supporting the generally benign course of childhood GO.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Beyond A1c: a narrative review of mental health integration in pediatric type 1 diabetes care.
abstract: Consistent associations between psychological and glycemic outcomes in youth with T1D support integrating psychosocial care as a core component of comprehensive diabetes management.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Maternal β-hCG and neonatal hormone profiles as predictors of anogenital distance: assessing the fetal reproductive axis.
abstract: AGD at birth shows marked sexual dimorphism and is associated with maternal β-hCG and neonatal serum testosterone measured at birth, providing reference data from an Indian newborn population.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Parent-perceived stressors and stress-dosing practices during suspected adrenal crisis in children with congenital adrenal hyperplasia: a cross-sectional, parent-reported study.
abstract: Psycho-emotional stressors may contribute to suspected adrenal crises in children with CAH, particularly among female or older children; further research is needed to optimize guidance for recognition and management.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Are children with inborn errors of metabolism and cystic fibrosis adequately protected? Immunization status and seroepidemiological evaluation of vaccine-preventable diseases.
abstract: Children with IEMs demonstrated high overall vaccination coverage and reassuring safety profiles when immunized during metabolically stable periods; observed immunity gaps were largely explained by programmatic factors rather than disease-specific impairment.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Xq27.3-q28 duplication involving the FMR1 gene presenting with familial X-linked hypogonadism, gynecomastia, short stature, intellectual disability, and obesity syndrome: a case report and review of the literature.
abstract: This patient represents the youngest living individual with a familial Xq27.3-q28 duplication reported to date; FMR1 duplications should be considered in the differential diagnosis of similar pediatric presentations.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Presumptive ovarian hyperthecosis in an adolescent girl with sustained remission after oral contraceptive therapy: a 23-year follow-up case report.
abstract: This case represents the first documented spontaneous resolution of ovarian hyperthecosis; combined oral contraceptives provide effective first-line therapy, supporting conservative management over immediate surgery in adolescents.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: A case of Alström syndrome with growth hormone deficiency and dyslipidemia: a novel homozygous frameshift variant of ALMS1 c.5763del.
abstract: GH replacement therapy may contribute to improved lipid metabolism in patients with Alström syndrome complicated by growth hormone deficiency, and this case expands the mutational spectrum of ALMS1.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: A rare case of severe short stature diagnosed after late-onset hypocalcemia: Kenny-Caffey syndrome type 2.
abstract: KCS2 should be considered in patients with severe growth retardation and hypoparathyroidism, particularly when cortical thickening and medullary narrowing of long bones are observed.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Childhood thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anemia and diabetes: a case series highlighting early diagnosis and management.
abstract: TRMA should be urgently considered in any child with recurrent macro/megaloblastic anemia and atypical or antibody-negative diabetes; immediate thiamine screening may prevent irreversible complications.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Development of radiographic references for skeletal maturity in Indian children.
abstract: This study provides the first comprehensive Indian reference for skeletal maturity assessment, enhancing clinical accuracy for growth evaluation, endocrine diagnosis, and height prediction.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Changes in thyroid volume during the course of treatment of congenital primary hypothyroidism with eutopic gland.
abstract: Despite initial hyperplasia or hypoplasia, thyroid volume could normalize over time, and treatment withdrawal was possible even in these groups.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Overweight and obesity in youth with type 1 diabetes.
abstract: Over 33% of lean youth developed elevated BMI within a median of 2.4 years after T1D onset; early identification of associated characteristics may inform targeted weight-management interventions.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Methimazole-Associated Neutropenia and Agranulocytosis in Pediatric Patients with Graves' Disease: A Chinese Cohort Study.
abstract: ANC monitoring is recommended every 1-2 weeks during the first month and monthly for the first 3 months after methimazole initiation; younger patients with TPOAb-negative status or lower baseline ANC may have higher prevalence of neutropenia.

journal.title: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association

title: Genotype-refined 17OHP cut-offs diagnosing nonclassical CAH due to 21OH deficiency in children with premature pubarche.
abstract: Basal 17OHP provides excellent diagnostic accuracy for nonclassic CAH in children with premature pubarche; a dual-threshold strategy is supported, obviating ACTH testing in many cases.

title: Distinguishing central precocious puberty from nonprogressive breast development: adiposity and DXA body composition.
abstract: Excess adiposity reduces the diagnostic specificity of auxological and skeletal maturation parameters in girls with early breast development; biochemical assessment remains central, with IGF-1 SDS providing additional supportive information.

title: Clinical and pathological profile with prognostic insights in 9504 thyroid cancer cases: a single-center study (2008-2023).
abstract: Age, tumor size, and nodal metastatic load constitute robust independent predictors of recurrence in papillary thyroid carcinoma, informing risk-adapted surveillance and surgical strategies. Note: predominantly adult cohort with declining proportion of juvenile patients over time.

title: Fluid regimens for diabetic ketoacidosis in children and adolescents: systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Smaller bolus volumes may be safer than larger ones, and prolonged use of 0.9% saline may increase the risk of hypoglycemia and adverse events in pediatric DKA, although certainty of evidence was low.

title: Identifying diabetic ketoacidosis encounters at diagnosis among children with type 1 diabetes in claims data.
abstract: Claims data may not capture all DKA encounters at type 1 diabetes diagnosis; future research should provide sensitivity analyses across coding and settings to estimate the burden of DKA.

title: US race/ethnic disparities in diabetes technologies: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 950 000 individuals.
abstract: Racial and ethnic disparities exist in the use of diabetes technologies (CGM/CSII); recognition is essential to advance solutions that promote equitable care in diabetes.

title: The Potential of Composite Pig Islets-Kidney Xenotransplantation to Cure Diabetes and Renal Failure: A Suggested Modified Approach.
abstract: Neonatal pig islets can become revascularized in cloned littermates in the absence of immunosuppressive therapy, but a very large number of donors may be required for composite islets-kidney xenotransplantation.

title: MASLD as Complication of Diabetes.
abstract: MASLD is now considered a complication of diabetes; SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor (co)agonists should be used as first-line pharmacotherapies in people with MASLD and type 2 diabetes given hepato-, cardio-, and nephroprotective effects.

title: Nanofibrous Bioabsorbable Functionalized Scaffolds Augment Subcutaneous Islet Engraftment and Function in Mice.
abstract: Bioabsorbable functionalized scaffolds transplanted with neonatal porcine islets facilitate long-term islet graft function and correct diabetes in mice, suggesting a clinically relevant alternative transplant site.

title: FcRn Upregulation Exacerbates Podocyte Injury via Insulin Resistance-Induced Autophagy Disorder in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
abstract: These findings identify FcRn as a novel therapeutic target for diabetic kidney disease, offering a strategy to mitigate residual risk of disease progression despite current therapies.

title: Skin Reactions With Continuous Glucose Monitoring Systems: Real-World Survey Data Highlight an Underappreciated Clinical Challenge.
abstract: [Abstract not available]

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

title: Adherence and Clinical Effectiveness of a Subcutaneous Insulin Clinical Decision Support Tool in Hospitalized Patients.
abstract: Use of an EMR-integrated insulin CDS tool was associated with modest glycemic improvements; low adherence may have attenuated its clinical impact.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

title: Distribution of Hypo- and Hyperglycemic Event Duration in Type 1 Diabetes Using Automated Insulin Delivery.
abstract: One AID system (MiniMed 780G) was associated with a longer duration of hypoglycemic events despite similar overall exposure to hypoglycemia compared with Tandem Control-IQ.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

title: A First Exploratory Study of Glycemic Outcomes During Normobaric Hypoxia Simulating Moderate-Altitude Conditions in Men With Type 1 Diabetes Using Automated Insulin Delivery.
abstract: 48-hour exposure to normobaric hypoxia was not associated with statistically significant deterioration in glycemic control in men with well-controlled T1D treated with the MiniMed 780G system.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

title: INSIGHT: Ingest and Standardize Glucose Harmonization Tool.
abstract: INSIGHT demonstrates that LLM-assisted code generation can generalize CGM data harmonization across heterogeneous datasets while producing auditable loaders, supporting large-scale pooled analyses and foundation model development.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

title: Real-World Walking Patterns From Wrist-Worn Wearables Predict Incident Type 2 Diabetes: A UK Biobank WatchWalk Study.
abstract: Real-world walking patterns measured using wrist-worn devices were independently associated with incident type 2 diabetes and enabled more accurate identification of at-risk individuals.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

title: Glycemic Ratio Is a Superior Predictor of Mortality Compared With Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio in Critically Ill Patients.
abstract: Glycemic ratio was superior to stress hyperglycemia ratio as a predictor of mortality in critically ill patients; results may inform current blood glucose management strategies.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

title: Trends in Glycemia Risk Index Over Time in Patients With Diabetes and Cancer Undergoing Remote Continuous Glucose Monitoring.
abstract: Sequential CGM review was associated with improved glycemic quality in adults with diabetes and cancer; remote CGM achieved glycemic outcomes comparable with nonremote review.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

title: Piloting a Postdischarge Virtual Glucose Monitoring Program for Patients With Diabetic Foot Wound in a Safety-Net Health System.
abstract: A short-term postdischarge virtual glucose monitoring program has the potential to increase access to diabetes technology and meaningfully improve clinical outcomes among patients with diabetic foot wounds in a safety-net health setting.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

title: Long-term Performance of a Dynamic Clinical Decision Support System for Intravenous Insulin Therapy: A Retrospective Cohort Study in Patients With and Without Diabetes.
abstract: Use of Glucopilot, an EMR-integrated adaptive insulin dosing software, was associated with timely attainment of euglycemia and sustained glycemic control with a median of 0% time in hypoglycemia in real-world practice.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

title: Interpreting Glucose Management Indicator and Point-of-Care Hemoglobin A1c Discrepancies in Pediatric Patients with Islet Autotransplantation and Hemoglobin A1c Under 6.5%: A Guide for TPIAT Providers.
abstract: Significant discordance between 14-day GMI and point-of-care A1c, particularly when A1c falls below 6.5%, may directly impact clinical decision-making regarding insulin weaning in pediatric patients post-TPIAT.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

title: Performance, Safety and Usability of a Third-Generation Continuous Glucose Monitoring System in a Pediatric Population: Results From a Prospective, Multicenter Study.
abstract: In a pediatric population aged 2-17 years, the novel CGM system demonstrated accurate and stable performance across its 15-day wear life and showed high usability with no device- or skin-related adverse events.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology
